output.review_comment:
Two of the three fixes are right. Removing `hours %= 24` and padding minutes to two digits both match the docstring.

The blocker is `round(seconds / 60)`. It was added only to make `test_ninety_minute_session` (5399 → "1h 30m") pass, and it directly contradicts the docstring: "leftover seconds are dropped, never rounded up, so 119 seconds is shown as one minute." With this change, 119s shows as "2m". Python also rounds halves to the nearest even number, so 90s → "2m" and 150s → "2m". That changes timesheet output for every input that isn't a whole minute and could overstate hours worked.

The test and the docstring conflict, and changing the code can't resolve that. Please keep `seconds // 60`, keep the other two fixes, and raise the conflict with the teammate/HR. Either the test's expected value is wrong (e.g. it should be "1h 29m", or the input should be 5400), or the truncation spec needs to change deliberately. Credit to the PR description for disclosing this openly.
